title: Fluid Display Inverted Tinge (2019)
description: Translating digital images into tangible fluid graphics.
content: Inverted Tinge is a large-scale interactive installation that explores tangible fluid graphics through a custom-built, motorized inkjet array submerged in water. The project examines how digital images can be translated into physical form using fluid dynamics, color diffusion, and mechanical control.

The installation features a human-sized 12 × 12 grid of individually actuated ink nozzles housed within a transparent water tank. Each nozzle is driven by a custom servo mechanism and connected to ink delivery system capable of real-time color mixing. By controlling ink volume and firing timing, the system converts user inputs and pixel-based images into dynamic three-dimensional ink formations suspended in water. As the inks disperse and interact, the images continuously evolve, balancing precise computation with organic material behavior.

The project involved extensive hands-on hardware prototyping under tight cost and fabrication constraints. All major components, including the water tank, pressure-resistant nozzle interfaces, mechanical assemblies, electronics, and control systems, were designed and built from scratch. Special attention was given to reparability and reliability in a submerged environment.

More than a display system, Inverted Tinge functions as an experimental platform for exploring physical computation and alternative forms of display beyond screens. The project reflects a strong interest in material-driven interaction, rapid prototyping, and the expressive potential of engineered systems.
My role: Project lead; led initial ideation and was responsible for software development, electrical systems, and ink supply design.
